title: make repin can pin a local build of a commit that is gone
foundBy: session agent, after rewriting unpushed history left store entries for commits no branch holds

evidence.verified: tests/test_repin_go.py passes all 7 of its tests against this same scripts/repin-go.sh. They pin and name a newer local build, and take CI's under `LOCAL=0`, when CI's is newer, and on a tie. They hold a build awaiting images, and skip one whose commit left the branch. In a scratch workspace, campaign's copy left out sandbox's newest local build once the sandbox checkout beside it held that commit on no branch. It said so, and took the build CI had made. GitHub CI's `ci` passed on 7f94c70.

resolution: A local build counts only if its commit is on a branch of the sibling's own checkout beside the consumer, where there is one. A newer build left out that way is named. Without such a checkout, as in a campaign member, the store is taken as it stands.
details: `scripts/repin-go.sh` takes the newest local build in the store whatever its commit. After a rebase or a squash, the store still holds builds of the commits that were replaced, and they carry the newest times. So `make repin` can pin a commit that no branch of the sibling's checkout holds any more, and its push is then held.
